questions.question: Ravi is younger than Sohan but older than Meena. Arjun is older than Ravi but younger than Karan. Who is the youngest?

Karan > Arjun > Ravi.

From the relationship Sohan > Ravi > Meena, we know that Sohan and Ravi are older than Meena.

From the second relationship,

Karan > Arjun > Ravi,

We know that Karan and Arjun are also older than Ravi.

Since Ravi is older than Meena, it follows that Meena is younger than Ravi, Sohan, Arjun, and Karan.

Therefore, Meena is the youngest person mentioned.

Hence, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

questions.question: Citizenship provisions are given in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part II** of the **Indian Constitution** comprises **Articles 5 to 11**, which govern the legal framework for **Citizenship** in India.
 
• These provisions specifically identified the persons who became citizens of India at the **commencement of the Constitution** on **January 26, 1950**, based on parameters like domicile, migration, and origin.
 
• **Article 11** is a significant provision that empowers the **Parliament of India** to make any law regarding the **acquisition and termination** of citizenship and all other related matters.
 
• Exercising this constitutional power, the **Parliament** enacted the **Citizenship Act of 1955**, which provides a comprehensive set of rules for citizenship after the initial constitutional phase.
 
• India adopts the principle of **Single Citizenship**, a concept borrowed from the **British Constitution**, which ensures that all citizens have the same rights across the entire nation, regardless of the state in which they reside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part I** of the Constitution includes **Articles 1 to 4** and deals with **The Union and its Territory**, outlining the territorial jurisdiction and the power to form or alter states.
 
• **Part III** encompasses **Articles 12 to 35**, which enumerate the **Fundamental Rights**, the basic civil liberties guaranteed to individuals to protect them from the arbitrary exercise of state power.
 
• **Part IV** contains **Articles 36 to 51**, representing the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are non-justiciable guidelines for the state to establish social and economic democracy and a **Welfare State**.
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** defines five ways to acquire citizenship: **Birth**, **Descent**, **Registration**, **Naturalization**, and **Incorporation of Territory**, while also providing for its loss through **Renunciation**, **Termination**, and **Deprivation**.

questions.question: Who has the power to create new states and alter boundaries of existing states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 3** of the **Constitution of India**, the power to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing states is vested solely in the **Union Parliament**.
 
• This authority allows **Parliament** to increase the area of any state, diminish the area of any state, or change the name of any state through a simple legislative process that does not require a complex constitutional amendment.
 
• A bill for the reorganization of states can be introduced in either **House of Parliament** (the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**) only after receiving the **prior recommendation of the President**.
 
• Before making such a recommendation, the **President** must refer the bill to the concerned **State Legislature** to express its views within a specified timeframe, although these views are **not binding** on the **Union Parliament**.
 
• The **Parliament** can proceed to pass the bill by a **simple majority** of the members present and voting, reflecting the **unitary bias** of the Indian federal system regarding territorial integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 2 and Article 4**

 
 
• **Article 2** empowers **Parliament** to admit or establish new states into the **Union of India** that were not previously part of its territory.
 
• **Article 4** clarifies that laws made under **Article 2** and **Article 3** are not to be considered amendments to the **Constitution** under **Article 368**, ensuring the process remains flexible.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Entities**
 
 
• **President of India**: Acts as a facilitator by providing the mandatory prior recommendation for the bill but does not possess the legislative power to alter boundaries independently.
 
• **State Legislature**: Its role is strictly **consultative**; it cannot block the **Parliament** from redrawing boundaries even if it disagrees with the proposal.
 
• **Supreme Court**: While the **Judiciary** can exercise **judicial review** over the legality of the process, it has no power to create states or define territorial limits.
 
 
 
• **Indestructible Union**
 
 
• India is often described as an **indestructible Union of destructible states** because the **Parliament** can change the political map of the country at its discretion without the consent of the states.

questions.question: Which deity is predominantly worshipped through Manipuri dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manipuri Dance**, also known as **Jagoi**, is one of the eight major **Indian classical dance** forms, originating from the northeastern state of **Manipur**.
 
• While the dance form has ancient roots in the pre-Hindu festival of **Lai Haraoba**, its classical identity is predominantly centered on **Vaishnavism**, which focuses on the devotion to **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The most significant theme in the Manipuri repertoire is the **Raslila**, a divine dance-drama that depicts the eternal love and spiritual connection between **Radha** and **Krishna**.
 
• The performance is characterized by its **Lasya** style, emphasizing gentle, fluid, and circular movements that reflect a meditative and devotional state (**Bhakti**) rather than dramatic or aggressive posturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context**:

 
 
• The formalization of the **Vaishnavite** Manipuri dance is largely attributed to **King Bhagyachandra** (reigned 1763−1798), who codified the **Raslila** after having a spiritual vision of **Krishna**.
 
• He introduced the unique **Kumil** costume, a stiff, barrel-shaped skirt decorated with gold and silver embroidery and mirrors, designed to hide the dancer's leg movements and create a gliding effect.
 
 
 
• **Role of Shiva and Other Deities**:
 
 
• **Shiva** is worshipped in the ancient **Lai Haraoba** tradition as **Nongpok Ningthou**, alongside **Parvati** (Panthoibi), representing the older indigenous beliefs of the **Meitei** people.
 
• Despite these older roots, the **classical** form recognized today focuses almost exclusively on the life of **Krishna** as narrated in the **Bhagavata Purana** and the **Gita Govinda** by **Jayadeva**.
 
 
 
• **Rhythmic Elements**:
 
 
• The **Pung** (a traditional drum) is central to the dance; the **Pung Cholom** is a masculine performance where dancers play the drum while performing acrobatic jumps and turns.

questions.question: Which of the following plate boundaries formed the Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convergent boundary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas** were formed as a result of the collision between the **Indo-Australian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**.
 
• This tectonic interaction began approximately **40 to 50 million years ago** during the **Cenozoic Era**, leading to the closure of the **Tethys Ocean** that once existed between the two landmasses.
 
• A **convergent boundary** occurs where two tectonic plates move toward each other. In the case of the Himalayas, it is specifically a **continent-continent collision**.
 
• Because both continental plates have relatively low density, neither could be easily **subducted** into the mantle. This caused the crust to thicken and fold upward, creating the world's highest **mountain range**.
 
• The process is still ongoing today, as the **Indian Plate** continues to move northwards at a rate of about **5 cm per year**, causing the Himalayas to rise and making the region highly **seismically active**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Divergent Boundary**:

 
 
• Characterized by plates moving away from each other.

• Because the time taken to rotate (**sidereal day**) is longer than the time taken to orbit (**orbital period**), a day on Venus is technically longer than its year.
 
• This unusually slow rotation is theorized to be the result of **solar tidal torques** acting on the planet's thick atmosphere, which gradually decelerated its spin over **billions of years**.

• **Solar Day vs. Sidereal Day**:
 
 
• While the **sidereal day** is 243 Earth days, the **solar day** (the time from one sunrise to the next) is only **117 Earth days** due to the combination of its retrograde spin and orbital path.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure**:
 
 
• The surface of Venus is characterized by an **extreme greenhouse effect** and a surface pressure **92 times** that of Earth, roughly equivalent to the pressure 1,000 meters underwater.

• **Uranus** possesses a highly unusual and irregular **magnetosphere**. Unlike most planets where the magnetic field is roughly aligned with the rotation, Uranus's magnetic axis is tilted at an extreme angle of **59 degrees** relative to its **rotational axis**.
 
• The magnetic field of **Uranus** is not generated from its geometric center; instead, it is **offset** by approximately **one-third of the planetary radius** (about 8,000 kilometers).
 
• This asymmetric magnetic field leads to a complex, twisting **magnetotail** that spirals behind the planet as it orbits the **Sun**.
 
• Data regarding these unique characteristics were primarily captured by the **Voyager 2** spacecraft during its historic flyby in **January 1986**.

questions.question: Blood is classified under which type of animal tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Connective tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood** is a specialized type of **fluid connective tissue** that plays a vital role in maintaining the body internal environment by circulating through the cardiovascular system.
 
• Biologically, it is classified as a connective tissue because it originates from the **embryonic mesoderm**, just like other connective tissues such as bone and cartilage.
 
• It consists of a straw-colored liquid extracellular matrix known as **plasma**, which constitutes nearly **55%** of the total blood volume, and **formed elements** making up the remaining **45%**.
 
• The **formed elements** are comprised of three main types of cells: **Erythrocytes** (Red Blood Cells) for oxygen transport, **Leukocytes** (White Blood Cells) for immune defense, and **Thrombocytes** (Platelets) for blood clotting.
 
• A unique characteristic of blood compared to other connective tissues is that its matrix is **fluid** and it lacks structural **fibers** like collagen or elastin under normal physiological conditions; however, **fibrin fibers** are formed during the process of **coagulation**.
 
• The primary functions of blood include the transport of **metabolic wastes** to the kidneys, delivery of **hormones** to target organs, and the regulation of **body temperature** and **pH levels**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epithelial tissue**:

 
 
• Forms the **outer covering** of the body and the **lining** of internal organs and cavities.
 
• Cells are tightly packed with minimal **intercellular space** and rest on a **basement membrane**.
 
 
 
• **Muscular tissue**:
 
 
• Comprised of elongated cells called **muscle fibers** that contain contractile proteins like **actin** and **myosin**.
 
• It is divided into three types: **skeletal** (voluntary), **smooth** (involuntary), and **cardiac** (heart muscle).
 
 
 
• **Nervous tissue**:
 
 
• Specialized for the **conduction of electrical impulses** throughout the body to coordinate functions.
 
• Main components include **neurons** (nerve cells) and **neuroglial cells** which provide support and insulation.

• **Chemotropism** is a biological phenomenon where the growth or movement of a plant part occurs in response to a **chemical stimulus**.
 
• In flowering plants, the growth of the **pollen tube** towards the **ovule** is a classic example of **positive chemotropism**.
 
• When a **pollen grain** lands on the **stigma**, it germinates to form a tube that travels through the **style**.
 
• The **ovule** secretes certain **chemical substances** (such as sugars or specific proteins) that act as attractants, guiding the **pollen tube** directly to the **embryo sac** for fertilization.

• The hormone **Auxin** facilitates this by promoting cell elongation on the shaded side of the stem.
 
 
 
• **Geotropism** (Gravitropism):
 
 
• This is the growth of plant parts in response to **gravity**.
 
• **Roots** typically exhibit **positive geotropism** by growing downwards into the soil, while shoots show negative geotropism.
 
 
 
• **Thigmonasty**:
 
 
• This is a **non-directional** movement triggered by **touch**, famously seen in the **Mimosa pudica** (Touch-me-not) plant.

• **Wheat**: Cultivation was encouraged in **Punjab** to ensure food security for the British army and for export to Europe.

⇒ Step 2: Calculate the **Square** of 11.6 → 11.6 × 11.6 = 134.56

⇒ Step 3: Calculate the product 4 × 9.8 × 1.8

⇒ 4 × 17.64 = 70.56

⇒ Step 4: **Subtract** the values: 134.56 − 70.56 = 64

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 336 square cm. One of the diagonal is 14 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus?

Use the **Area formula**: Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ ⇒ 336 = (1/2) × 14 × d₂ ⇒ d₂ = 48 cm.

Apply **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25) for the right triangle formed by half-diagonals: Side (a) = 25 cm.

**Perimeter** = 4 × side = 4 × 25 = 100 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

1) Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

2) Side (a) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

3) Perimeter = 4 × a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aa6b33389ef7ce441d183dc5038c431df5068e3d17b2c294d4a5105044b321b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 336 = (1/2) × 14 × d₂

⇒ 336 = 7 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 336 ÷ 7 = 48 cm

⇒ Half of diagonals: d₁/2 = 7 cm and d₂/2 = 24 cm

⇒ **Side (a)** = √[7² + 24²]

⇒ a = √[49 + 576] = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 25 = 100 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

questions.question: The adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio of 4 : 5. What are the measure (in degrees) of the larger angle?

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of **adjacent angles** is always 180°.

Given **ratio** = 4 : 5

9 units = 180° ⇒ 1 unit = 20°

**Larger angle** = 5 units = 5 × 20° = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

**Formula Used:**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the measures of the **adjacent angles** be 4x and 5x.

⇒ 4x + 5x = 180°

⇒ 9x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 9

⇒ x = 20°

⇒ Larger angle = 5x = 5 × 20° = 100°

⇒ Smaller angle = 4x = 4 × 20° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

Properties of Parallelogram

Opposite angles are always equal, and the sum of all interior angles is 360°.

Consecutive Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, consecutive interior angles (like adjacent angles in a parallelogram) are supplementary.

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The diagonals bisect each other but are not necessarily equal in length unless the figure is a rectangle.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** of an article are increased or decreased by the **same percentage**, the **Profit or Loss percentage** remains **constant**.

This occurs because the **ratio** between the Selling Price and Cost Price (SP/CP) does not change when both terms are multiplied by the same factor.

Initial loss = 30% ⇒ Final loss = 30%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 50 percent more than its cost price. If the profit earned is 25 percent, then what is the discount offered on the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio **CP : MP** = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

Ratio **CP : SP** = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5 (since **Profit** is 25%).

Equating **CP** in both ratios: **CP : SP : MP** = 4 : 5 : 6.

**Discount** = **MP** − **SP** = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

**Discount %** = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup Percentage** = 50%

**Profit Percentage** = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dc26fb84ab1848b1747f39efe5006fdcbbfd3751d25648132eaf9124ae41b0f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** + **Profit**

**Discount** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Selling Price (SP)**

**Discount %** = (**Discount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = 150 − 125 = 25.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (25 ÷ 150) × 100.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.666...%

⇒ **Discount Percentage** ≈ 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

Markup and Profit Relation

The relationship between **Marked Price (MP)** and **Cost Price (CP)** can be expressed as: **MP / CP** = (100 + **Profit %**) / (100 − **Discount %**).

Effective Discount Formula

For two **successive discounts** of a% and b%, the single **equivalent discount** is given by: (a + b − ab/100)%.

Profit and Discount Calculation

**Profit** is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**, whereas the **Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**.

questions.question: What is the fourth proportion of 18, 4 and 45?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Fourth Proportional (d)** of three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c** is given by the formula:

**d = (b × c) ÷ a**

Here, **a = 18**, **b = 4**, and **c = 45**.

⇒ **Fourth Proportional = (4 × 45) ÷ 18 = 180 ÷ 18 = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The three numbers are **18**, **4**, and **45**.

**Formula Used:** If four numbers **a**, **b**, **c**, and **d** are in **proportion**, then **a : b :: c : d**, which implies **a ÷ b = c ÷ d** or **a × d = b × c**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a02230afc780e3e9e51605aac50b3f8b7974230c8fb92f1ee75c4b98d78d4b6.png] 

Let the **fourth proportion** be **x**.

⇒ **18 : 4 :: 45 : x**

⇒ **18 ÷ 4 = 45 ÷ x**

⇒ **18 × x = 45 × 4**

⇒ **18x = 180**

⇒ **x = 180 ÷ 18**

⇒ **x = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

If **a**, **b**, and **c** are in **continued proportion** (**a : b = b : c**), then **c** is the **third proportional**, given by **c = b² ÷ a**.

Invertendo and Alternendo

If **a : b = c : d**, then **b : a = d : c** (**Invertendo**) and **a : c = b : d** (**Alternendo**).

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The newly constructed library will be inaugurated by the President of the university next week.

options.text: The President of the university inaugurates the newly constructed library next week.
The President of the university inaugurated the newly constructed library next week.
The President of the university will inaugurate the newly constructed library next week.
The President of the university has inaugurated the newly constructed library next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of the university will inaugurate the newly constructed library next week**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Indefinite Tense**. The passive structure for this tense is **Object + will be + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.

• To convert to **Active Voice**, the **Subject** of the passive sentence (The President of the university) must become the active subject that performs the action.

• The **Object** of the passive sentence (the newly constructed library) becomes the direct object that receives the action in the active sentence.

• The verb phrase **will be inaugurated** (passive) must be transformed into the **Future Indefinite Active** form, which is **will + Base Form (V1)**, resulting in **will inaugurate**.

• The time reference **next week** remains unchanged as it modifies the timing of the action in both voices.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Analysis of Incorrect Tense Options**:

• **Simple Present Tense**: Option 1 uses 'inaugurates', which is used for **habitual actions** or **general truths**. It does not reflect the specific future intent established by the passive 'will be'.

• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 2 uses 'inaugurated', indicating an action already **concluded in the past**. This creates a logical contradiction with the future time marker **next week**.

• **Present Perfect Tense**: Option 4 uses 'has inaugurated', signifying an action **just completed** or having present relevance. This tense cannot be used for scheduled events occurring in the **upcoming week**.

</ul

__

• The standard passive construction for a command or order is: **Let + Object + be + V3 (Past Participle)**.

• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the sentence must start with the **Base Form of the Verb (V1)**, followed by the **Object**.

• In this case, the verb **'vacated'** (V3) is changed back to its base form **'vacate'** (V1).

• The word **'let'** and the auxiliary verb **'be'** are removed, as they are markers of the passive imperative form.

• The **Object** **'the premises'** is placed immediately after the main verb, and the **Adverb** **'immediately'** remains at the end to maintain the original meaning.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Imperative Sentences** and Voice Conversion:

• **Command/Order**: Sentences like 'Shut the door' (Active) become 'Let the door be shut' (Passive).

• **Requests**: If the active voice includes **'Please'**, the passive voice uses the construction **'You are requested to...'**. Option 1 is incorrect because the original sentence does not contain 'please' or indicate a request.

• **Subject in Active Imperatives**: In the active imperative form, the subject **'You'** is always **omitted** but understood by the reader or listener.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
Neither the chairman nor the members of the committee was able to find a solution to the pressing issue.

options.text: was able to find out a solution
were able to find a solution
had been able to find for a solution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the correlative conjunction **Neither... nor** to join two subjects: **the chairman** and **the members**.
 
• According to the rule of **subject-verb agreement**, when subjects are joined by **either... or** or **neither... nor**, the verb must agree with the **closest subject** (the second subject).
 
• In this sentence, the second subject is **the members of the committee**, which is **plural**.
 
• Therefore, the singular verb **was** must be replaced with the plural verb **were** to ensure grammatical correctness.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Neither the chairman nor the members of the committee **were able to find a solution** to the pressing issue.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Proximity Rule:** This rule states that the verb should agree with the noun or pronoun closest to it when using connectors like **or**, **nor**, **either... or**, and **neither... nor**.
 
• **Option 1:** **was able to find out a solution** – Incorrect because it retains the singular verb **was**.
 
• **Option 3:** **had been able to find for a solution** – Incorrect because the phrase **find for** is idiomatically wrong in this context; the verb **find** does not require the preposition **for** when looking for a result.
</ul

सही उत्तर है- **__कोर्ट द्वारा दिया गया निर्देश__**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **अदालती आदेश** का शाब्दिक अर्थ **न्यायालय** या **कोर्ट** द्वारा किसी मामले के संदर्भ में दिया गया आधिकारिक **निर्देश** अथवा **आदेश** होता है।
 
• कानूनी भाषा में, जब न्यायाधीश किसी पक्ष को कुछ करने या न करने का निर्देश देते हैं, तो उसे **कोर्ट ऑर्डर (Court Order)** कहा जाता है।
 
• यह आदेश लिखित या मौखिक हो सकता है, जिसका पालन करना संबंधित पक्षों के लिए अनिवार्य होता है।
 
• उदाहरण के तौर पर: **'The judge issued a court order to stop the construction.'** (न्यायाधीश ने निर्माण कार्य रोकने के लिए एक **अदालती आदेश** जारी किया।)

 कानूनी शब्दावली की विशेषताएं-

 
• **शुद्धता:** कानूनी शब्दों का अर्थ अत्यंत **सटीक** और स्पष्ट होता है।
 
• **निश्चितता:** इन शब्दों का प्रयोग किसी विशेष **कानूनी संदर्भ** में ही किया जाता है।
 
• **पारिभाषिक शब्दावली:** ये शब्द सामान्य बोलचाल से भिन्न, **प्रशासनिक** और **न्यायिक** कार्यों के लिए आरक्षित होते हैं।

इसका सही उत्तर '**आंतरिक सुरक्षा**' है। 

**__Key Points__**

**गद्यांश के अनुसार,**

__
 
• यह गद्यांश किसी क्षेत्र की **सुरक्षा व्यवस्था** के मुख्य केंद्र, यानी **थाने** पर केंद्रित है।
 
• इसमें **पुलिसकर्मियों** की भूमिका, **शिकायत दर्ज करने** की प्रक्रिया और **नागरिकों की सहायता** के बारे में बताया गया है।
 
• चूँकि पुलिस और कानून-व्यवस्था का मुख्य कार्य देश या समाज के भीतर शांति और व्यवस्था बनाए रखना है, इसलिए यह विषय सीधे तौर पर **आंतरिक सुरक्षा** से संबंधित है।
 
• अतः, सही उत्तर **आंतरिक सुरक्षा** है।

**Additional Information__**

**अन्य विकल्पों का विश्लेषण:**

 
• **खेल:** गद्यांश में किसी खेल, खिलाड़ियों या खेल प्रतियोगिताओं का कोई संदर्भ नहीं है।
 
• **पर्यटन:** गद्यांश किसी यात्रा, ऐतिहासिक स्थल या घूमने-फिरने की गतिविधियों के बारे में जानकारी नहीं देता है।
